Simulate a steady-state, two-phase (oil–water) flow in a horizontal pipe using twoPhaseEulerFoam.
Use a pipe with a diameter of 0.05 m and a length of 3 m, long enough for the flow to reach a developed state.
Discretize the pipe with a body-fitted or block-structured mesh, with sufficient radial resolution to capture the near-wall and interphase regions.
Impose a fixed mixture velocity of 1 m/s at the inlet as a fixedValue condition on both phase velocities.
Impose alpha.water = 0.3 at the inlet as a fixedValue condition in 0/alpha.water.
Set the outlet boundary for alpha.water to zeroGradient.
Set appropriate zeroGradient/fixedValue (pressure and flux-consistent) outflow conditions for velocity and pressure at the outlet.
Apply noSlip to the pipe walls for both phases.
Use water with a density of 1000 kg/m^3 and a dynamic viscosity of 1e-3 Pa·s.
Use oil with a density of 800 kg/m^3 and a dynamic viscosity of 3e-3 Pa·s.
Treat the flow as turbulent using a kEpsilon turbulence model applied per phase, consistent with the turbulent Reynolds number of the chosen velocity and geometry.
Use the Schiller-Naumann drag correlation for the oil–water interfacial momentum exchange in constant/interfacialProperties.
Treat the oil as the dispersed phase in the continuous water phase, consistent with alpha.water = 0.3.
Run the transient solver until a statistically steady, developed state is reached, and verify convergence of the phase distribution and velocity profiles.
Document all chosen parameters (geometry, velocity, properties, turbulence model, drag model) that were not explicitly fixed by the requirements.
